issues.kind: a reader restates law 1 (4) without the strip margin its term 'the ends' carries; two readings, one breaking law 1 (4)
issues.owner: pipeline (§4.4 S5a Trace (2); §4.3 Where it may not go); END model (§2.7's worked examples)
issues.claim: Law 1 (4) (l. 2721-2723) keeps an enclosing wall's line, band and wall strips off a raised way's ENDS, and the terms (l. 2617-2618) define the ends as 'its ramps, stairs and feet, each widened by the same margin' (raisedWays.structure.stripMarginM, 1 m); §5.3's law-1 row (l. 9943) checks law 1 (4) as the laws state it. The one list of a trace's impassables at §4.4 S5a Trace (2) (l. 6602), which S3 (9)'s and S5a's pulls, every epoch circuit, contraction and re-anchored stretch (V06 §3.7.4 (2), §3.7.6 (5)), a dossier-admitted circuit and a hand contractWall take and which *beneath* now cites for its widenings (l. 3074-3080), reads 'a standing raised way's ramps, stairs and feet widened by the wall strips' width there'; §4.3 Where it may not go (l. 6503), the course rule of every aqueduct laid after a standing wall, reads 'its ramps, stairs and feet off the band and wall strips'; and §2.7's examples restate it (*Line and band* l. 3069-3070, *Where the line crosses* l. 3058-3059, *over the band* l. 3016). The same texts elsewhere use the ends (S5a's pin rule l. 6603, S3 (7) l. 6227, V06 §3.19 (5), the fixed-place sentence l. 3260-3261 'widened by the strip margin'). A build of the list and of §4.3 as written buffers the bare ramp, stair or foot, so a pull or cost field hugging that impassable lays its wall strips inside the strip margin round an end, and an aqueduct course stands its end's margin under a standing wall's setback or glacis: law 1 (4) broken, §5.3's law-1 row failing the build (E_INVARIANT). One reading of a builder's text breaks a law-1 invariant: not a valid choice (J151), as the first fix pass graded the same list's missing over-crossing spans (VF7-GEN-01).
issues.required_change: pipeline: §4.4 S5a Trace (2), the one list (l. 6602): "a standing raised way's ramps, stairs and feet widened by the wall strips' width there," -> "a standing raised way's ends (its ramps, stairs and feet widened by `raisedWays.structure.stripMarginM`, §2.7's laws' terms) widened by the wall strips' width there (law 1 (4)),". pipeline: §4.3 *Where it may not go* (l. 6503): "its ramps, stairs and feet off the band and wall strips" -> "its ends (its ramps, stairs and feet widened by `raisedWays.structure.stripMarginM`, §2.7's laws' terms) off the band and wall strips". END model, §2.7's worked examples: *Line and band* (l. 3069-3070): "the line kept from a ramp, stair or foot by the wall strips' width there (law 1 (4))" -> "the line kept from a raised way's ends (a ramp, stair or foot widened by the strip margin, these laws' terms) by the wall strips' width there (law 1 (4))"; *Where the line crosses* (l. 3058-3059): "its band and wall strips kept off them too (law 1 (4))" -> "its band and wall strips kept off its ends too (law 1 (4))"; *over the band* (l. 3016): "and its ramps, stairs and feet kept by its course off the band and the wall strips (law 1 (4);" -> "and its ends (its ramps, stairs and feet widened by the strip margin) kept by its course off the band and the wall strips (law 1 (4);". Each seat's sweep (R7-01 (2)) conforms any other restatement naming a ramp, stair or foot where law 1 (4) reads the ends.

issues.kind: two readings of one list; the doubled reading gives way where law 2 (a) lays a lawful shape
issues.claim: The one list (l. 6602), as adjudication-r7w P2 wrote it: 'every held building's strip and a shape-locked raised way's `vault`-use spans' strips, each widened all round by the wall strips' width there (law 1 (10): ...)'. A held building's strip is by definition already the span's strip 'widened all round by the meeting wall's strips' width' (terms, l. 2642-2643), and §2.7's examples keep a pulled line out of it once (*A held building in an arch vault* l. 3124-3128: 'a trace laid by the pull or a cost field treats it as impassable'; *Line and band* l. 3073-3074: it 'count[s] the band's half already'). Read distributively, 'each' widens it a second time (the pipeline seat noted both readings, repair-r7w-pipeline.md), and *beneath* now takes the list's widenings as stated (l. 3078-3079). The doubled reading keeps law 1 but bars a further 12-24 m (§4.8 l. 8351, 8354) round each held building's span; where the only lawful crossings within the pull's search band or an epoch circuit's reach lie there, the doubled build takes law 2 (c) (F-WALL's raised-way rung, l. 9855, else an unwalled stage; at an epoch walls.waited) where law 2 (a) lays a lawful trace - breaking law 2 (a)'s '(a) fails where none lies within that reach' (l. 2813), the outcome Part P pass 8 ruled against J144 as the program reads it (PRB7H-GEN-04 (i)) and adjudication-r7w held no valid choice (VF7v-GEN-03, -06). T110-2 (4)'s held-building circuit (l. 19451-19456) does not separate the builds.
issues.required_change: pipeline: §4.4 S5a Trace (2) (l. 6602): "every held building's strip and a shape-locked raised way's `vault`-use spans' strips, each widened all round by the wall strips' width there (law 1 (10): no line, band or wall strip across one)" -> "every held building's strip (widened by its own definition, §2.7's laws' terms; law 1 (9)) and the strip of each `vault`-use span of a shape-locked raised way widened all round by the wall strips' width there (law 1 (10): no line, band or wall strip across one)".

issues.claim: Fixed at *Where the line crosses* (l. 3061-3063) and the bent group's lawful crossing (l. 3180-3182); the column that reads the state still says, C5 (l. 3273-3274), 'a trace laid after a support is `cleared` passes through its ring as open ground', and W1·C5 (l. 3340) and W3·C5 (l. 3342) repeat 'through a `cleared` ring as open ground'. Law 1 (2) (l. 2705-2713) reads each span's soffit standing or fallen and admits over only with every span above the band clearing the wall's top; a band wider than the ring lies under the two fallen spans beside it. The bars carry the condition (adjudication-r7w C7, C8); §5.3's law-1 row catches a build from the column: minor.

issues.claim: Law 1 (10) (l. 2739-2743) bars a wall-like line, band or strip newly across the strip of a shape-locked raised way's `vault`-use span; wall strips are 'across' (l. 2644-2645). The bent-group sentence's strip is the under-deck strip widened by the band's half 'together with every held building's widened strip that meets it' (l. 3176-3178), and its moves put the line on that strip's edge ((i)'s path l. 3198-3199, (ii) l. 3203, (iii) l. 3205), where the deck-side wall strip reaches into the under-deck strip by its setback (6-20 m, §4.8 l. 8351, 8354), far past the 1 m margin and across the spans beside it. M4 conditioned only the lawful crossing (l. 3185-3187); the strip and its long sides (l. 3187-3188) omit a shape-locked raised way's `vault`-use spans, so a stretch drawn along beneath one, or moved along its strip to a lawful crossing, is laid by the example with its wall strip across them; §5.3's law-1 row catches it (T110-2 (4)'s along-beneath clause over the C8 shape-locked state, l. 19279-19281, 19441-19445): minor.
issues.required_change: model: the bent-group sentence (l. 3176-3178): "together with every held building's widened strip that meets it (*beneath*)," -> "together with every held building's widened strip, and the strip of each `vault`-use span of a shape-locked raised way widened all round by the wall strips' width there (law 1 (10)), that meets it (*beneath*),"; and (l. 3187-3188) "each passing outside every held building's widened strip on its side;" -> "each passing outside every held building's widened strip and every such widened span strip on its side;".

issues.kind: law wording; two readings, one excluded by law 3's own lead
issues.owner: model (END-L, the laws' home; Part L l. 614-615 with it)
issues.claim: Law 3 (l. 2855-2856): 'A line's part inside a strip that crosses no deck line there goes to the strip's edge on the side it entered from.' *The strip* is the under-deck strip (l. 2614-2615); a line on its edge leaves half its band inside it, which law 1 (4) (l. 2721-2723) bars (and, for a shape-locked raised way, its wall strip across the `vault`-use spans beside it, law 1 (10)). Law 3 ranks only 'the lawful shapes law 2 (a) or (b) leaves open' (l. 2844), so the literal place is never among them and the sentence can only choose the side, as the bent-group example reads it (l. 3176-3178); every build that passes the check takes the entry side's nearest lawful place: minor. The fix removes words (J150).
issues.required_change: model, END-L: law 3: "goes to the strip's edge on the side it entered from" -> "leaves it on the side it entered from" (Part L l. 614-615 likewise).
